A Massachusetts pharmacist who does not practice CDTM has completed 13 eligible CE contact hours for 2026. All applicable live, pharmacy-law and specialized-topic requirements are already satisfied. On December 30 she attends nine hours of ACPE-approved CE, including two hours of pharmacy law, during one calendar day.

Which entry records the maximum eligible conference credit and her resulting 2026 total? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Claim 8 conference hours and record a 2026 total of 21 hours.
Claim 7 conference hours and record a 2026 total of 20 hours.
Claim 9 conference hours and record a 2026 total of 22 hours.
Exclude the two law hours, claim 6 conference hours, and record 19 hours for 2026.

records.stem:
A Massachusetts physician telephones a community pharmacy with a new Schedule IV prescription. The pharmacist on duty can supervise and has approved an eligible technician to receive the call. Four employees have current Massachusetts personnel licenses: Mara's national certification expired yesterday; Eli has current Board-recognized national certification; Noor is a pharmacy technician trainee; and Jon is an ordinary pharmacy technician with 15 years of experience and no national certification.

Which employee may receive this new prescription under the technician scope rules? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Mara, whose state technician license remains active.
Eli, whose state license and national certification are current.
Noor, acting under the pharmacist's direct supervision.
Jon, based on his documented experience as a licensed technician.

records.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacy is preparing an adult influenza clinic under a valid standing order. A qualified immunizing pharmacist will counsel patients, select each vaccine and directly supervise administration. Two fully licensed technicians have current CPR certification and completed the ACPE six-hour technician course, including two hours of live injection training.

Alex is not nationally certified, has worked 520 hours after full technician licensure, and has completed 90 minutes of documented on-the-job training with an experienced certified immunizer. Blake holds current PTCB certification, has worked 300 hours after full technician licensure, and has completed two additional documented on-the-job hours with an experienced certified immunizer. Both have completed a skills checklist. All other applicable conditions are satisfied.

Which staffing assignment is permitted now? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Assign Alex to prepare and administer vaccines; Blake must first reach 500 post-licensure hours.
Assign Blake to prepare and administer vaccines; Alex needs further on-the-job training.
Assign both technicians because the six-hour course includes the required workplace training.
Assign neither technician until each holds national certification and has 500 post-licensure hours.

records.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacy receives two otherwise valid Schedule III prescriptions, each written for a 56-day supply in one filling. One is buprenorphine/naloxone for an adult's established opioid-use-disorder treatment. The other is BUTRANS (buprenorphine) transdermal patches for a different adult's established chronic-pain treatment. Neither involves an implantable infusion pump. All other prescribing and dispensing requirements are met; the pharmacist is reviewing the Massachusetts day-supply limit for a single filling.

Which supply plan fits that limit? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Allow a 56-day single filling for both prescriptions.
Allow 56 days for the OUD prescription; limit the pain prescription to no more than 30 days in one filling.
Limit the OUD prescription to 30 days; allow 56 days for the pain prescription.
Limit both prescriptions to 30 days in one filling.

records.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacy receives a valid electronic prescription issued November 2, 2026 by a Massachusetts physician for 60 Schedule II methylphenidate tablets. The pharmacy has all 60 in stock. On November 9 the adult patient requests 20 tablets. During a consultation at 10:00 a.m., the prescriber authorizes 20 tablets per partial dispensing under that prescription. No quantity has yet been dispensed.

Which actions or conclusions apply to this requested-partial-fill pathway? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Record the later authorization as 'Authorized by Practitioner to Partial Fill,' with the practitioner's name, discussion date and time, and pharmacist's initials.
Dispense 30 tablets if the patient changes the request, because the original prescription authorizes 60 in total.
Start the remainder's 30-day filling period on November 9, when the first partial dispensing occurs.
At the patient's request, the same pharmacy may dispense another 20-tablet partial quantity on November 25 while the prescriber's plan remains in effect.

records.stem:
On November 2, 2026, a HIPAA-covered Massachusetts pharmacy discovers one reportable breach of unsecured PHI affecting 620 individuals: 310 reside in Massachusetts and 310 in Rhode Island. The pharmacy has current mailing addresses for all affected individuals. There is no law-enforcement delay or other notice exception.

Which notification plans comply with the federal breach-notification rules? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Notify the affected individuals without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery.
Notify HHS contemporaneously with the individual notices for this breach.
Notify prominent media outlets in both states because the breach affects 620 individuals in total.
Log the breach for HHS submission within 60 days after the end of 2026 instead of using the contemporaneous reporting route.

records.stem:
A Massachusetts physician's electronic prescribing system temporarily fails. The physician has prepared a valid, properly signed paper prescription for oral immediate-release oxycodone, and a courier can deliver the original to the pharmacy before the patient needs the first dose. The adult patient is not in a long-term care facility or hospice, and the prescription is not for parenteral infusion. The patient asks the retail pharmacist to dispense before the courier arrives. The clinic can also fax an image of the prescription now.

Which dispensing plan is lawful under these facts? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Accept an emergency oral order and dispense now because the electronic system is unavailable.
Dispense now from the faxed image and file the original when the courier arrives.
Receive the original signed paper prescription and dispense after the usual validation.
Require a new electronic prescription after the system is restored, despite the valid paper original.

records.stem:
On November 4, 2026, River Pharmacy receives a valid oral estradiol prescription, classified in Massachusetts Schedule VI, and a valid electronic testosterone prescription, classified in Schedule III. Both are for lawful gender-affirming care. The same verified prescriber, Dr. Elena Lee of Harbor Health Practice, requests that the practice name replace her individual name on the patient labels. The pharmacy is filling the prescriptions for the patients; the prescriber is not dispensing medication directly. All other prescription and labeling conditions are satisfied.

Which proposed label or record actions are correct? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Print 'Harbor Health Practice' in the estradiol label's prescriber-name field in response to Dr. Lee's request.
Print only 'Harbor Health Practice' as the prescriber on the testosterone label as well.
Keep Dr. Lee's actual identity in the original prescription records for both orders.
Replace River Pharmacy's name and address on the estradiol label with Harbor Health Practice's name and address.

records.stem:
At 4:00 p.m. on Friday, November 6, 2026, a DEA-registered retail pharmacy discovers a confirmed theft of controlled substances. The inventory reconciliation will finish on Thursday, November 12. Monday, November 9 is the next business day; no holiday affects it.

Which proposed steps meet the federal DEA reporting requirements for this theft? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Send the initial written notice to the local DEA Field Division Office on Monday morning, November 9, while reconciliation continues.
Set December 21, 2026 as the latest date for submitting the complete and accurate electronic DEA Form 106.
Wait until November 12 to send the initial written notice so that it includes the final inventory count.
Use December 24 as the Form 106 deadline if the initial written notice is sent on November 9.

records.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacy stores unopened LANTUS 10-mL vials in a monitored refrigerator at 5°C; their manufacturer expiration date is ten months away. During counseling, one patient reports keeping a LANTUS SoloStar pen at 23°C since first using it ten days ago. Another patient has kept an opened LANTUS 10-mL vial at 5°C since first using it ten days ago. None of the products has frozen or been exposed to excessive heat or light.

Which storage or discard instructions follow the product labeling and Massachusetts storage policy? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Keep the unopened vials refrigerated at 5°C and use their manufacturer expiration date if proper storage continues.
Refrigerate the opened SoloStar pen at 5°C between uses while keeping its 28-day discard date.
Discard the in-use SoloStar pen 28 days after first use, even if insulin remains.
Move the opened vial to room temperature because LANTUS labeling prohibits refrigerating an in-use vial.
